page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, positioning it as a compute-focused resource. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates solid mid-range performance. It achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1402.0 and a multi-core score of 8470.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 19226.97. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 831.5 GB/sec, which drops to 84.73 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance handles database operations effectively, registering 7793.61 on PassMark database benchmarks and sustaining 15.82 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. For lightweight machine learning tasks, it processes 1247.06 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M LLM model, though performance drops to 32.03 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration represents a clear tradeoff, requiring external storage configuration and limiting its utility for heavy deep learning or high-intensity graphics tasks. However, its dedicated CPU allocation and high multi-threaded decompression throughput make it a cost-efficient option for raw compute tasks. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, text processing, and medium-scale database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute-focused server instance featuring 16 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs (8 physical cores) and 32.0 GB of RAM. Operating at 2.5 GHz, this KVM-hypervised instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results indicate balanced mid-range capabilities, with a PassMark CPU score of 19226.97 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 8470.0. It demonstrates strong utility for database operations, achieving 15.82 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, and handles static web serving at 16.69 GB/sec. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a resource-efficient choice for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local disk I/O. It is highly suitable for web serving, software compilation, and moderate database workloads.
